chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman who gives herself to her husband in exchange for release, or who pays him to divorce her (khal'), with the testimony of two witnesses regarding her purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse. Does she become fully divorced (tabin) from him by that, or is she still his wife as long as the divorce has not followed? He said: She becomes fully divorced. If he wishes, he can return to her what he took from her, and she remains his wife, and he may do so. I said: It has been narrated that she does not become fully divorced until the divorce follows her. He said: That is not the case if it is a khal'. I said: She becomes fully divorced? He said: Yes. The reason in this narration, likewise, is what we previously mentioned: interpreting it as being based on taqiyya (dissimulation). And his saying 'That is not the case if it is a khal'' means in their view. And the meaning is not that it is not a khal' in our view. And that which reveals what we said regarding the exit of that from the realm of taqiyya.
ai.seo_question: Does a woman become fully divorced immediately after paying her husband for khal' in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes that in the Shia view, *khal'* results in an immediate, irrevocable separation (*tabin*) upon the wife's payment and witness testimony, contrasting with the Sunni position which often requires a subsequent divorce pronouncement. The Imam resolves the apparent contradiction with other narrations by attributing them to *taqiyya*, thereby affirming the distinctiveness of the Shia legal stance on marital dissolution. This ruling underscores the finality of *khal'* as a complete severance of the marital bond rather than a preliminary step.
